text:
nina: hitting a weird combo on Fedora 36 when trying to run `redwoodctl local serve` after installing via the distro package. service starts but bind fails with permission denied. journalctl shows `Permission denied` on /run/redwood/socket.

omar: distro package probably drops a systemd user unit that expects the socket dir under /run/user/$UID. SELinux could block the bind if the executable label is wrong. what does `sestatus` say?

nina: SELinux is enforcing. `ausearch -m avc -ts recent` shows denies for redwoodctl trying to create `unix_stream_socket`.

tess: we've seen this for packaged installs. Workarounds: 1) run `redwoodctl local serve --unix-socket /tmp/redwood.sock` or `--host 127.0.0.1` 2) relabel the binary context with `chcon -t bin_t $(which redwoodctl)` (not ideal) 3) prefer the official tarball and run from your home dir which has a permissive label.

nina: switched to `--host 127.0.0.1` and it worked. but follow-up: after creating a new profile via `redwoodctl profiles create ci-keeper` and adding token, subsequent `redwoodctl local serve` picks up an older `default` profile even though `profiles list` shows `ci-keeper` as active.

omar: is there a `REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH` set in your environment or a system-wide `/etc/redwood/config.yaml`? CLI prefers explicit env var over user config.

nina: aha there was `/etc/redwood/config.yaml` with `current_profile: default`. removed it and now CLI respects the user-level `current_profile`.

tess: note for DX: installer should not create a system config without asking. filing DX-610. also add a `redwoodctl profiles sync` command to detect and warn when system/user envs conflict.

qa-bot: created issue DX-610: installer.system-config-question and DX-611: profiles-sync-warning.

nina: one more quirk — our CI rotates tokens daily via a job, and when the token for the active profile is rotated the CLI starts failing with `403: invalid_token` on local serve; I expected `redwoodctl` to auto-refresh or at least show a clearer hint.

omar: auto-refresh is tricky for static tokens. we do have `redwoodctl profiles rotate --profile ci-keeper --token <new-token>` to update tokens programmatically. For CI you can export `REDWOOD_TOKEN` in the job and avoid storing the token in file.

tess: UX idea: `redwoodctl local serve` could detect 401/403 and print an inline hint: "token expired? run `profiles rotate` or set REDWOOD_TOKEN". filing DX-612.

ops-bot: scheduled small patch to CLI to improve expired-token hints (PR #2239) - target v0.12.5.

nina: thanks all. summarizing workaround steps I used: 1) run with `--host 127.0.0.1` to avoid SELinux/socket denies 2) check and remove `/etc/redwood/config.yaml` if present 3) prefer env `REDWOOD_TOKEN` for ephemeral CI tokens or use `redwoodctl profiles rotate` to update profile tokens.

qa-bot: added Nina's summary to devex/cli/troubleshooting.md. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
